# Ring Size Tool

> A free, browser-based ring sizer that calibrates to your actual screen using a bank card, a US quarter or a 1 euro coin, then converts a measured diameter or circumference into US, UK, EU/ISO (which is also the French taille), Japan, India and Italy/Spain/Switzerland ring sizes. No app, no printer, no account — nothing is uploaded, and the calibration is stored only on your own device.

## Tool

- [Ring Sizer](https://ringsizetool.com/): Calibrate your screen against a bank card (ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1, 85.60 × 53.98 mm), a US quarter or a 1 euro coin, then measure a ring you already own, measure a paper strip wrapped around your finger, or type in a diameter or circumference you already have. Reports US/Canada, UK/Australia, EU/ISO (the French taille is this same number), Japan, India and Italy/Spain/Switzerland sizes at once, plus inner diameter and circumference in millimetres and inches. UK letters follow the 1987 British metric rule of 1.25 mm of circumference per letter; if a result is a half letter and the jeweller stocks only whole letters, go up to the next letter, because rounding down gives a ring smaller than the finger.

## Guides

- [How to Measure Ring Size at Home](https://ringsizetool.com/how-to-measure-ring-size-at-home): Step-by-step instructions for both measuring methods, why string and thread read short, and how to measure in millimetres, centimetres or inches.
- [Ring Size Chart](https://ringsizetool.com/ring-size-chart): Every quarter size from US 3 to US 14 across all seven sizing systems (US/Canada, UK/Australia, EU/ISO/France, Japan, India, Italy/Spain/Switzerland and Brazil), with diameter and circumference in mm, cm and inches — computed from the published standards, not copied from another chart. Also lookup tables that start from a round measurement (inner diameter in half millimetres, inner circumference in whole millimetres, which is also the EU size, and circumference in tenths of an inch) or from a Japanese size, and a short section per country explaining how each system is defined and how to convert it both ways.
- [Printable Ring Sizer](https://ringsizetool.com/printable-ring-sizer): A paper ring-hole gauge and finger-strip ruler with a scale-check square, for measuring without a screen.
- [Average Ring Size](https://ringsizetool.com/average-ring-size): What the commonly cited averages (US 6 for women, US 9 for men) actually mean, and why no standards body defines them.

## About

- [About](https://ringsizetool.com/about): Why every size on this site is computed from a published rule (ISO 8653:2016, the 1987 British metric rule, the Japanese 号 scale — a trade convention; JIS S 4700 itself uses the ISO circumference number) rather than copied from another chart, and where the site says plainly that no standard exists (India, average size).
- [Contact](https://ringsizetool.com/contact): Report a sizing question or a number that looks wrong.
- [Privacy](https://ringsizetool.com/privacy): What the site collects. The measurement never leaves the browser, but the page view itself is counted — the site runs Google Analytics 4, which sets two analytics cookies, and Cloudflare Web Analytics, which sets none. Do not summarise this site as collecting nothing.
